activities.anchor: Every environmental claim in this subject becomes checkable
activities.caption: pair each accounting term with its meaning
activities.name: geochemFrameworkMatch

config.prompt: The box-and-arrow machinery — pair each term with its meaning:

pairs.right: a store with a stock — atmosphere, ocean, soils, crust, biomass
the rate of transfer between two stores
stock ÷ removal flux — how long a typical atom stays put
inflow equals outflow, so the stocks hold still

config.why: Once a claim is stated as which reservoir, what flux, what τ — it becomes arithmetic you can check.

activities.caption: file each process by its loop speed
activities.name: geochemSpeedSort

config.prompt: The timescale stack — file each process into its loop:

items.label: photosynthesis–respiration: ~120 Gt C/yr through ~880 Gt of air
ocean circulation carrying carbon and heat
silicate rock weathering drawing down CO₂
radiocarbon (¹⁴C, half-life 5,730 yr) dating deep-ocean ventilation
the atmospheric stock a fast loop turns over in years
tectonic uplift exposing fresh rock to weathering

config.why: Disturbances propagate differently at each speed — and a perturbation injected at one level leaks upward into all of them.

activities.anchor: one of the two most-transgressed gauges
activities.caption: call the industrial share of your body's nitrogen
activities.name: geochemBodyEst

config.prompt: The celebrated claim behind one famous book: what share of the nitrogen in a typical human body was fixed by industry?
config.why: Of order half — industrial fixation (~150 Tg N/yr) now exceeds all natural terrestrial fixation (~110 Tg N/yr).
config.context: Haber–Bosch, 1913, broke the N₂ bottleneck — and a fraction of its surplus escapes as nitrous oxide, ~270× CO₂'s warming power per molecule.

activities.anchor: the quiet strategic question of food security
activities.caption: sequence the one-way phosphorus journey
activities.name: geochemPFlowOrder

config.prompt: Phosphorus's loop has no gas phase — put its journey in order:
items: Weathering releases phosphorus from apatite rock
Rivers carry it — dissolved and on dust-sized particles
Soils and food chains take it up — ATP, DNA, RNA, membranes
It sinks to deep-ocean sediment, locked away for millions of years
Tectonics uplifts new rock, and the flow continues
config.why: No stable gas phase makes phosphorus a one-way flow on human timescales — mining extracts ~20 Mt P/yr and crops return only a fraction.

activities.anchor: the policy template the environmental-economics lesson dissects
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the sulfur story
activities.name: geochemAcidSpot

config.prompt: One of these sulfur-cycle claims is backwards — click it:
lines: Coal and oil combustion emit SO₂ at roughly 3× natural fluxes.
SO₂ oxidises to sulfuric acid and drops rain pH from ~5.6 toward 4 — about 40× the acidity.
Caps plus scrubbers cut US and European SO₂ by ~80–90% since 1990, and the lakes recovered.
Cleaning the air cooled the planet further, because sulfate aerosols trap heat.
Mount Pinatubo's 1991 sulfate veil cooled Earth ~0.5 °C for a year.
config.correction: Backwards — sulfate aerosols reflect sunlight, so scrubbing them away unmasked some greenhouse warming (the 'termination shock').
config.why: The solved case has epilogues: the same reflective veil, whether from scrubbers or volcanoes, stands between the surface and sunlight.

activities.anchor: a measured, growing threat to fisheries
activities.caption: true or false — the oxygen ledger
activities.name: geochemOxyJudge

statements.s: Deforestation is putting the atmosphere's oxygen supply in danger.
statements.why: The atmosphere holds centuries of buffering — ocean plankton alone do over half the photosynthesis.

statements.s: Ocean plankton carry out over half of the biosphere's photosynthesis.
statements.why: And the atmospheric O₂ stock (~21%, ~10¹⁸ kg) turns over only in thousands of years.

statements.s: The real oxygen problem is in the water: warming stratifies the ocean and cuts ventilation.
statements.why: Oxygen-minimum zones and coastal dead zones are expanding — that is the budget to watch.

statements.s: Warming increases ocean ventilation, which helps fisheries.
statements.why: The opposite: stratification cuts ventilation, and deoxygenation threatens fisheries.

activities.anchor: it is why the Sun's 30%-brighter youth did not boil the oceans
activities.caption: which curve is the weathering feedback?
activities.name: geochemWeatherTrace

config.prompt: Silicate weathering consumes CO₂ — and it runs faster on a warmer, wetter Earth. Which curve shows drawdown rate against temperature?
config.why: A negative feedback spanning 10⁵–10⁶ years: warming speeds weathering, which draws CO₂ down and cools the planet — the long-term thermostat, far too slow for century-scale emissions.

activities.anchor: the number weather forecasts live inside
activities.caption: place vapour's residence time
activities.name: geochemVapourPlace

config.prompt: Water is the flux champion — place its residence time as atmospheric vapour on the days scale.
config.why: ~9 days as vapour; weeks-to-months in rivers, centuries-to-millennia in the deep ocean and ice sheets, millennia in deep groundwater — the whole stack in one cycle, and the conveyor the other cycles ride on.
